contentPolicy: Original FluentPath familiarisation tasks covering representative IELTS Academic and PTE Academic question types. These are not official or copied exam questions; educator review is required before sale.

tasks.title: Reading · Identify claims and information
tasks.instructions: Read the short passage. Decide whether each statement matches the information or the writer's view.
tasks.passage: A university tested a weekend shuttle between two campuses for twelve weeks. Passenger counts rose on Saturdays, although the study did not compare every possible reason for the increase. The writer argues that another trial should include more months and a wider range of students before the route becomes permanent. The report does not state how much the shuttle cost to operate.

questions.question: The shuttle trial lasted twelve weeks.
questions.explanation: The first sentence states that the trial lasted twelve weeks.

questions.question: The report proves the shuttle was the only reason passenger numbers rose.
questions.explanation: The report says it did not compare every possible reason.

questions.question: The writer supports making the shuttle permanent immediately.
questions.explanation: The writer recommends a broader trial before a permanent decision.

tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Match headings and details
tasks.instructions: Read the three short paragraphs and select the heading, paragraph, or researcher that matches each question.
tasks.passage:
A. The town opened a repair café where residents bring small appliances and learn basic repairs from volunteers. Organisers say the sessions also create a place for neighbours to meet.

B. A local survey found that many residents wanted evening sessions, but the survey included only people who had already visited the library. The council plans a second survey in other neighbourhoods.

C. Researcher Maya Chen recommends measuring how many items are repaired and how many residents return. Researcher Omar Ali says transport access should be improved before adding more sessions.

questions.question: Which heading best describes Paragraph A?
options: A shared place to learn repairs
A survey with a limited sample
questions.explanation: Paragraph A describes repair practice and neighbour contact.

questions.question: Which paragraph mentions a limitation in the survey sample?
questions.explanation: Paragraph B explains that only previous library visitors were surveyed.

questions.question: Who recommends measuring repeat visits?
questions.explanation: Maya Chen recommends measuring how many residents return.

tasks.rights: Created for this project; not official exam material

tasks.title: Reading · Complete ideas from a passage
tasks.instructions: Read the passage and choose the ending that completes each idea accurately.
tasks.passage: A college introduced a lending library for laboratory equipment. Students can borrow tools for short projects instead of buying them. The first review found that bookings were highest near assignment deadlines. Staff also found that clear return dates reduced missing equipment. The college plans to keep the service and review its storage space next year.

questions.question: Students can use the lending library to…
questions.explanation: Students borrow equipment rather than buy it for short projects.

questions.question: Bookings were highest…
options: on the first day of term
questions.explanation: The first review found peak bookings near deadlines.

questions.question: The college plans to review…
questions.explanation: The final sentence states that storage space will be reviewed.

tasks.title: Reading · Complete a summary
tasks.instructions: Read the passage and type the missing word or short phrase. Check spelling before submitting.
tasks.passage: A coastal research team restored a small salt marsh by reopening a channel that had been blocked by an old embankment. Native plants returned over two growing seasons. The team measured water levels and plant cover each month, but warned that one site cannot predict results everywhere. Long-term monitoring will continue because storms and nearby construction may affect the marsh.

questions.question: The team reopened a ______ that had been blocked.
questions.explanation: The restoration reopened a channel.

questions.question: Native plants returned over two ______ seasons.
questions.explanation: The passage specifies two growing seasons.

questions.question: Why will monitoring continue?
options: Storms and nearby construction may affect the marsh
The team has already studied every coastal site
The plants need to be removed
questions.explanation: The final sentence names storms and construction as possible influences.

tasks.title: Reading · Follow a process and locate details
tasks.instructions: Use the passage to complete the labels and answer in a few words.
tasks.passage: In a small water-reuse system, rain first enters a storage tank through a roof pipe. A mesh screen removes leaves before the water reaches a settling chamber. After heavier particles sink, the water passes through a sand filter. The treated water is stored separately and used for garden irrigation; it is not intended for drinking.

questions.question: Roof pipe → storage tank → mesh screen → settling chamber → ______ filter
questions.explanation: The passage says water passes through a sand filter.

questions.question: What is the treated water used for?
questions.explanation: The treated water is used for garden irrigation.

questions.question: Is the stored water intended for drinking?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says it is not intended for drinking.

tasks.format: Multiple Choice, Multiple Answers · Highlight Correct Summary
tasks.title: Listening · Identify the main points
tasks.instructions: Listen to the short talk. Select the two supported details, then choose its best summary.
tasks.audioScript: A city tested reflective paint on the roofs of three public buildings. Measurements showed lower roof temperatures on sunny afternoons, but indoor temperatures changed less consistently. The team says the trial is promising but small, and it will compare different materials over a full year before making recommendations.

questions.question: Which TWO findings did the speaker report?
options: Roof temperatures were lower on sunny afternoons
Indoor temperatures changed consistently in every building
The trial included three public buildings
The team has already made a final recommendation
questions.explanation: The trial involved three buildings and found lower roof temperatures on sunny afternoons.

questions.question: Choose the best summary of the talk.
options: A small roof-paint trial showed a promising result, but the team wants a year of comparisons before recommending a material.
The city replaced every roof and confirmed indoor temperatures always fell.
The team rejected all reflective materials before taking measurements.
questions.explanation: The speaker describes a promising small trial and plans a year-long comparison.

questions.question: What will the team compare next?
options: Different materials over a full year
questions.explanation: The team plans to compare materials over a full year.

tasks.passage: A campus pilot collected rainwater from two laboratory roofs. The stored water was used for garden irrigation after a basic filtration step. The report found that collection varied substantially between months, so the system could not supply every garden throughout the year. The authors recommend adding a larger storage tank only after another year of measurements.

questions.question: Which TWO statements match the passage?
options: Rainwater was collected from two laboratory roofs.
The stored water was used for drinking.
The authors recommended installing a larger tank immediately.
questions.explanation: The passage says two roofs were used, and collection varied between months. It does not describe drinking use or immediate tank expansion.

questions.question: Why did the authors recommend further measurement?
options: The current supply was uneven across the year.
The filtration step was never used.
questions.explanation: The system could not supply every garden all year because collection varied.

questions.question: What would the authors consider after another year of measurements?
questions.explanation: They recommend considering a larger tank only after another year of measurements.

tasks.instructions: Write one sentence that summarises the main idea and key information in the passage.
tasks.prompt: Community science programmes invite residents to collect observations about local wildlife. These observations can cover a wider area than a small research team could visit alone. However, results are most useful when volunteers receive clear instructions and researchers check unusual records. A recent project found that short training sessions improved the consistency of reports, although participation varied between neighbourhoods. The authors recommend combining volunteer data with regular expert surveys rather than treating either source as complete on its own.
